faq.q: Why does it show two different categories for my BMI?
faq.a: It reports both the WHO international bands (normal 18.5–24.9, overweight 25–29.9, obese ≥30) and the Asian/Indian cutoffs (normal 18.5–22.9, overweight 23–24.9, obese ≥25) side by side. The same number can read as normal on one and overweight on the other — a BMI of 24 is normal by WHO but overweight under the Indian thresholds the tool shows.

faq.q: What are the BMR, TDEE and body-fat figures based on?
faq.a: BMR uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation from your weight, height, age and sex; TDEE multiplies it by your chosen activity level (1.2 sedentary up to 1.9 very active). Body fat uses the US Navy formula if you enter waist, neck (and hip for women), otherwise a BMI-based Deurenberg estimate. It also gives Devine and Robinson ideal weights and waist-to-height/waist-to-hip ratios.

The medical disclaimer also notes BMI ignores muscle mass, bone density and fat distribution and is not a diagnosis.

faq.q: Does it keep my previous readings?
faq.a: Yes. Each calculation is saved to a history list in your browser (up to 12–15 entries), and your last inputs are restored next visit. You can reload any past reading, download a text report, or export a CSV of all readings. Repeated identical clicks aren't stacked, so the history reflects genuine changes in weight.
